items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: And I played this festival and this band was Andrew Hill, Bobby Hutcherson, Ron Carter, Roy Hanyes, Joe Henderson and myself.

ctx.x: Yeah. I know you’ve got a long list of people here, some of them being saxophone players also, you’ve played beside Joe Henderson.

Um hum. I did a great concert, I had a great concert with him. This band was an awesome band to be a part of. There was a drummer that I had worked with, but he was great, he and my Uncle George had worked together a lot. And he worked with Sonny Rollins for many, many, years, his name is Eddie Moore. And Eddie in the musical community is one of the very revered musicians. And Eddie, after he died there was a festival out in California that they do every year, and they named it after him, the Eddie Moore…

I guess so. Here’s a kind of a hard question I think, but are you a type of improviser that thinks of technical things while you’re playing as far as here comes this chord, I know what scales and everything goes with it and I can choose — I mean is it possible to talk about what you think about when you’re improvising?
